whatIs.title: Betting?
whatIs.description: Arbitrage betting is a sports betting strategy that takes advantage of different odds offered by multiple sportsbooks for the same event. By placing calculated bets on all relevant outcomes, bettors can potentially create a position where the combined odds provide a favorable return, regardless of which outcome wins.

exploreStrategies.title: Betting Strategies
exploreStrategies.description: Arbitrage betting can take several forms depending on the number of outcomes, sportsbook prices, and timing of the wager. Understanding these approaches can help bettors recognize potential opportunities and choose the right odds for each position.

cards.title: 2-Way Arbitrage Betting
cards.description: Two-way arbitrage covers markets with two possible outcomes, such as moneyline bets in certain sports or over/under markets. Bettors compare prices across sportsbooks and look for odds that can cover both outcomes.

cards.title: 3-Way Arbitrage Betting
cards.description: Three-way arbitrage applies to markets with three possible outcomes, commonly including soccer match results: home win, draw, or away win. Different sportsbook prices are compared to identify potential pricing discrepancies across all three outcomes.

cards.title: Cross-Sportsbook Arbitrage
cards.description: Cross-sportsbook arbitrage involves comparing odds offered by multiple sportsbooks for the same event and market. Differences in pricing can create potential arbitrage opportunities when the combined implied probabilities meet the required conditions.

cards.title: Live Sports Arbitrage
cards.description: Live arbitrage involves evaluating changing odds while a sporting event is in progress. Since prices can move quickly, opportunities may appear and disappear within a short period.

cards.title: Pre-Match Arbitrage
cards.description: Pre-match arbitrage focuses on opportunities available before an event begins. Bettors have more time to compare sportsbook lines, calculate positions, and evaluate the available prices.

legality.title: Legal?
legality.description: Arbitrage betting is generally not prohibited as a betting strategy. However, its legality depends on the gambling laws and licensed betting options available in the bettor’s jurisdiction. Regulations can also differ between states, provinces, or territories.

faq.description: Find answers to common questions about arbitrage betting, sportsbook odds, opportunities, calculations, legality, and how Unbound can help streamline your betting workflow.

items.question: How does Arbitrage Betting work?
items.answer: Bettors compare sportsbook odds, identify suitable price differences, calculate their stake allocation, and place bets across the relevant outcomes.

items.question: Is Arbitrage betting profitable?
items.answer: Arbitrage opportunities can potentially produce a positive return when the required odds and stake calculations remain valid. However, odds can change, bets can be rejected, and sportsbooks may impose limits.

items.question: Is Arbitrage betting legal?
items.answer: The legality of sports betting depends on your location and local gambling regulations. Always use licensed sportsbooks permitted in your jurisdiction.

items.question: Can Unbound help me find arbitrage opportunities?
items.answer: Unbound helps users scan sportsbook boards, compare odds, identify potential arbitrage opportunities, and evaluate positions before betting.

items.question: How is Unbound different from an odds sports arbitrage scanner?
items.answer: A basic odds sports arbitrage scanner primarily helps identify pricing differences. Unbound extends the workflow by helping users calculate opportunities, document actual bets, and track their results.
